name: YES3 Exporter II
description: The successor to the original YES3 Exporter launched in 2022. Key features include a horizontal layout for longitudinal projects, with one column per event per field. It supports tab- or comma-delimited formats, payloads that include export-specific data dictionaries and data distribution summaries, and can generate ready-to-run SAS code tailored to each export for interactive or batch use.

versions.comments: Ordering of forms and fields corrected in export editor selection dropdowns. Special handling for checkbox field values without labels. Codebook popup added to main icon group.
Yes3Trait and Yes3Fn reconciled. Bug fix for repeating instruments in non-longitudinal projects: redcap_repeat_instance was not included in exports.
Minor tweaks to SASCoder, Editor UI improvements.
Removed Yes3ValuesetIndexer, a few UI tweaks.
Major SAS code generator improvements. SAS formats now shared across all exports. Better z-index handling for inline help popups, triggered by dragging.

versions.description: fine tuning, almost ready for prime time
versions.comments: Inline help largely completed. Auto loading 'getting started' panels. All help panels resizable and movable.

versions.comments: Inline help largely completed. Auto loading 'getting started' panels.

usability improvements, bug fixes, new options
versions.comments: New 'remove unprintables' option. Data dictionary export now excel-friendly csv. Data exporter refactored for efficiency and performance (unbuffered generator, uses record cache for selection).

The YES3 Exporter II perfoms a number daily tasks for each project. By default all of the daily tasks are run at 11 minutes past midnight, but you may specify a different time to run these tasks.

DAILY EMAIL NOTIFICATIONS

You may elect to receive daily summaries of YES3 Exporter II actions by email.
Enable email notifications
Time email notifications were last sent successfully

HOST FILE SYSTEM EXPORTS

YES3 Exporter II can export to the host file system. This will require services from your REDCap host system administrator, and the blessing of your Information Security Officer.
Enable export to host file system
Host file system folder. This folder must be writable by the web server user, and is typically an automount bound to a secure external fileshare

ALLOW USER DOWNLOADS AS WELL AS FILE SYSTEM EXPORTS

You have enabled direct exports to your file system, but you may elect to allow user downloads as well. For security reasons we recommend that you do not allow user downloads in addition to filesystem exports.
Allow user downloads in addition to filesystem exports

ENABLE BATCH EXPORTS

You may enable automated batch exports. If you do, each export for which you have checked 'Include in batch export' will be run as part of the nightly Exporter cron job.
Enable automated (cron) batch exports

SAS CODE DEFAULTS

Your exports can be accompanied by execution-ready SAS code. In this section you may enter defaults for information required by the SAS code generator. These optional defaults may be overriden for any given export specification.
SAS libref (1-8 character library name; typically a shortened version of your project name)

SAS library path (full path to the directory where the SAS datasets and format libraries will be written). Note for Windows users: You must escape backslashes in file paths, e.g. (Z:\\mypath\\sascode) instead of (Z:\mypath\sascode)

BACKUP RETENTION

By default, 20 generations of each export specification are retained, and can be restored using the 'wayback' feature. You may change this number, or elect to retain all generations.
Specification backups to retain (default is 20)
